BLUEPRINT PRESS

The combination you asked for:

· Blueprint's drafting grid, now drawn in faint navy on light stock
· Swiss Grid's palette — off-white, near-black, one red accent
· Editorial Press's type — Instrument Serif over Spectral

One change I made on purpose: the 'black' is #0B1A2B, the blueprint navy, not a true black. It keeps the whole page faintly blue and lets the mark belong.

Hover anything. The nav is clickable.

THE MARK

The B's curves are now ONE unbroken stroke that starts at the top of the stem and ends at its base — out, back, out further, back. It never lifts.

The navy→blue gradient runs along that travel, so the eye follows the direction of flow.

Four containers to choose from, plus how it holds up at favicon size (it needs a heavier stroke and flat blue below ~24px).

MOTION & CONTROLS

Twelve live treatments — hover them, click the segmented toggle.

They all share one easing curve so the site feels like one hand made it.

Tell me which ones you want and I'll build those into the real components. 07 (flowing border) is the loudest; 01 and 08 are the ones I'd use everywhere.

The original five. A · Blueprint was the pick — its grid and its navy carried over into Blueprint Press on the first page.

Kept here for reference, and in case you want to pull anything else across.

A · BLUEPRINT  ← chosen

The work itself, as a drafting sheet: grid, title block, dimension lines, revision numbers.

The grid texture and the navy both survive into the final direction; the dark background did not.

B · EDITORIAL PRESS  ← type came from here

Instrument Serif over Spectral, hairline rules, the drop cap.

Tradeoff it carried: on its own it read more 'design portfolio' than 'engineer' — solved by keeping the blueprint grid underneath it.

C · MACHINED

Loud and physical: safety orange, hazard striping, Archivo Black, part-number tags.

Tradeoff: heavy and shouty. Great on a hero, tiring across a long resume page.

D · INSTRUMENT

An HMI / oscilloscope panel — mono throughout, readouts, status LEDs, a live scope trace.

Tradeoff: phosphor green is a big commitment, and the data density fights long prose.

E · SWISS GRID  ← palette came from here

Off-white stock, near-black ink, a single red accent.

Its strict 12-column layout stayed behind; the numbered section rails (01 Summary, 02 Experience) are the part that carried over.
